neighbours.label: clinical prognostic variables in medical outcome studies (positive surgical margins, hemodynamically stable, blood levels of)
fire: On multivariate analysis, positive lymph nodes and tumour size predicted shorter survival.
Patients who were hemodynamically unstable at arrival had higher thirty-day mortality.
Elevated blood levels of lactate were associated with worse outcomes in sepsis.
Recurrence was more common when resection margins were positive on pathology.
Low serum albumin at admission independently predicted poor overall survival.
Vascular invasion and high tumour grade were linked to reduced disease-free survival.
In the cohort, hemoglobin below ten grams per decilitre doubled the risk of death.
Five-year survival was lower among patients with positive surgical margins.
quiet: The hospital cafeteria now offers more vegetarian options for visitors.
Nurses on the surgical ward work twelve-hour shifts during the week.
Patients are encouraged to bring a list of their medicines to each appointment.
The clinic moved to a larger building near the train station last year.
Medical students spend two months on the oncology ward in their final year.
The surgeon explained the procedure to the family before the operation.
Many patients prefer morning appointments so they can go to work afterwards.
The new waiting room has comfortable chairs and plenty of natural light.

notes: Card: top = ' positive' (surgical margins), ' blood' (levels of haemoglobin), ' hem' (hemodynamically stable), 'era of modern therapies' in oncology/clinical outcome papers. Near misses keep medical topic but drop the prognostic-variable framing. Not probed.
